title: M0-T132 admission held: the Fable 5 seven-day usage cap is rejecting model calls, so the digest-keyed shell-routing evidence at 2.1.252 (e713c5a6) cannot be honestly captured; a repin+recert now cannot satisfy the owner's ONE-combined-recert-at-ONE-identity requirement (R441/R442) without a later R247-invalidating second recert
affects: M0-T132 (D-024 Amendment 34 combined 2.1.252 admission + single R247 recertification): three owner-named fixtures captured (benign version-only drift), but the manifest repin + one combined recert are held
detail: Fresh preflight PASSED (Bootstrap Gate 0 + R438: on-disk claude.exe = 2.1.252 e713c5a6 217406624 B byte-identical to versions/2.1.252; DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 inherited; DISABLE_UPDATES unset; --version 2.1.252; nothing newer staged; mcp empty; tree clean at 1d4a6212). The three owner-named fixtures (capability_probe, event_bus/hook_event_catalog, native_adapter) were captured live and show ONLY a benign version-string change: claude --help sha256 UNCHANGED (83af8a9a7edc), official hooks docs enumerate the SAME 33 events, native flags/verbs/background surface identical. THEN a live blocker surfaced: the shell-routing fixture (shell_routing/v1, R292/R295) is a BEHAVIORAL probe that runs the installed claude under a bounded deny-everything harness; two runs returned verdict=no_tool_observed, and instrumenting one run showed the cause is a hard usage cap - rate_limit_event status 'rejected' rateLimitType 'seven_day_overage_included', assistant text 'You've reached your Fable 5 limit', seven_day utilization 0.78. The bare claude invocation uses the default model (Fable 5), so the routing probe is capped and cannot produce a truthful native_preferred measurement at the new digest. shell-routing is digest-keyed and FOLDED into cli_capability_manifest (FOLDED_PROBES), so after a repin to e713c5a6 a real start needs fresh e713c5a6 routing evidence; the existing evidence is d6f6c29a (2.1.251) and would return routing_evidence_stale -> the start still fails closed. Decisive conflict: the owner authorized ONE combined R247 recert at ONE final frozen identity (R441/R442); R247 says any later supervisor-evidence change invalidates that certification and forces a re-run; a later shell-routing recapture at e713c5a6 IS such a change; so doing the recert now guarantees a SECOND recert later, violating 'one combined recert'. R221 forbids consuming owner Fable allowance to work around a quota event; R220 forbids blocking otherwise-provable work (the three fixtures DID proceed). Whether shell-routing is inside the owner's 'three affected fixtures' scope (it is a fourth, digest-entangled one; behavior unchanged but evidence invalidated by the digest change) is a genuine ambiguity the orchestrator must not resolve silently (directive-compliance section 3.9). Per R394 the orchestrator stopped without retry, preserved all evidence, deleted the capped-model artifact fixture (it would have false-greened the shell-routing gate, which accepts any measured fixture for the identity regardless of verdict), left the tree clean, and returns this ONE consolidated assessment. Full findings: project-control/reports/M0-T132-admission-evidence.md.
